title: Scrum Master Salary in 2026 (US, UK, Canada & Australia)
dek: There's no official government salary figure for Scrum Masters, so every number is self-reported. In the US they average roughly $123k–$127k (Indeed, Glassdoor); pay varies by country — about £54k in the UK, C$109k in Canada, and A$137k in Australia.

seo.metaDescription: What Scrum Masters earn in 2026 across the US, UK, Canada, and Australia — each source named, plus an honest note on why there's no official figure.

sources.label: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — Project Management Specialists (for comparison)

body.richText: Scrum Master pay looks generous — often six figures in the US — but there's an honesty problem most salary articles skip: no government statistics agency tracks "Scrum Master" as a distinct job. So unlike a project manager salary, every figure you'll see is self-reported to a salary aggregator. Here's the honest, country-by-country picture, with the source named for each number.

Read this first: the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics has an official occupation code for project managers but none for Scrum Masters. That means all the numbers below come from self-reported data (Glassdoor, Indeed and similar), not official statistics. Treat them as useful ranges, not precise facts.

In the United States, the two largest salary aggregators land close together. Indeed reports an average of about $123,000 per year (based on job-posting data), and Glassdoor reports an average of roughly $127,000, with a typical range from about $100,000 at the 25th percentile to $163,000 at the 75th. Entry-level Scrum Masters average closer to $80,000, and experienced or lead roles push well past $160,000.

body.richText: For contrast, the project manager role does have an official US median — $100,750 (BLS, May 2024). Interestingly, self-reported Scrum Master averages often sit above that, likely because Scrum Masters cluster in higher-paying tech and finance sectors. But remember you're comparing an official median with self-reported averages, which isn't a like-for-like comparison.

Don't compare these country numbers directly as if they were measured the same way. Currencies, cost of living, tax, and how each source defines the role all differ. Use each figure within its own country, and click the source for the current range.

items: Experience — by far the biggest factor; lead Scrum Masters can earn double an entry-level salary
Industry — aerospace/defense, financial services, and consulting tend to pay the most
Location — major tech hubs pay more, but usually cost more to live in too
Scope — coaching multiple teams or moving toward agile-coach and RTE roles raises pay
Real facilitation track record — the market has many certified Scrum Masters, so demonstrated experience is what commands the top of the range

body.richText: The biggest early jump is landing the Scrum Master title itself, not stacking more certificates. A certification opens the door; running real sprints and retrospectives is what moves you up the pay band.

items.question: What is the average Scrum Master salary in 2026?
items.answerRichText: In the US, self-reported averages are about $123,000 (Indeed) to $127,000 (Glassdoor) per year. Typical pay is roughly £54,000 in the UK, about C$109,000 in Canada, and around A$137,000 in Australia — all from the salary sources linked in this guide.
